item.text:
Overall, the 2024 record is strongly negative for 4B.9. I found selective platform blocking, content-removal pressure, mandatory data-sharing/retention rules, criminal cases for online criticism, and administrative retaliation against opposition offices. The only pro-freedom evidence is narrow and procedural: a delayed Constitutional Court ruling and a brief reduction in throttling.

|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|

This is limited judicial pushback against a censorship tool, but the ruling was delayed and did not stop 2024 restrictions. | 4B.9; 4B.6; 4B.4 |

That is only a narrow mitigating sign, not evidence of a genuinely protected online space. | 4B.9; 4B.6 |

It also notes mandatory traffic retention and user-data sharing obligations. | 4B.9; 4B.6; 4B.5 |

That is direct evidence of surveillance-backed chilling of political speech. | 4B.9; 4B.6; 4B.5 |

This is a direct digital-control measure used to pressure a platform. | 4B.9; 4B.6 |

That is administrative harassment of opposition-held local government, even though it is not digital-specific. | 4B.9; 4B.5; 4B.7; 4B.8 |

Search gap: I did not find credible 2024 reporting of a nationwide internet shutdown in Turkey. The pattern was narrower and still coercive: selective throttling, platform blocks, content removal, surveillance, and legal harassment.
